sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Democrats lead in Ohio, Iowa Senate races amid Trump unpopularity
cards.content: Widespread dissatisfaction with President Trump's handling of the presidency has opened up a prime Senate pickup opportunity for Democrats in Ohio and Iowa. In Ohio, Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown holds a 6-point lead over Jon Husted, a Republican former lieutenant governor, while in Iowa, the Senate race is a razor-thin contest. The poll finds that likely voters in both states mostly disapprove of Trump's handling of the presidency, say his policies have increased the cost of living, and are financially worse off than two years ago. Democrats are favored to win the governor's race in both states.

Elderly Woman Evicted from Madrid Home Dies Amid Nationwide Housing Crisis
cards.content: An elderly woman, Maricarmen Abascal, 87, who was forcibly evicted from her apartment in Madrid, Spain, has died. Her situation became a symbol of Spain's housing crisis, sparking nationwide protests and a political row that led to early elections. Abascal's eviction, which occurred on September 23, was met with widespread outrage and support from the public and celebrities. The government's attempt to push through urgent housing measures failed, prompting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to call snap elections. Her death has sparked a collective gasp and minute of silence at the Madrid square where protesters have camped demanding affordable housing.

cards.title: Bluefin Tuna Return to UK Waters After International Efforts
cards.content: Bluefin tuna have returned in huge numbers off the British coast after almost disappearing from UK waters, according to a major new report from WWF. The report highlights conservation successes, including a 73% decline in monitored wildlife populations globally since 1970. The return of bluefin tuna is attributed to concerted international efforts, including reduced catch quotas and protected spawning grounds. cards.title: Pioneering Software Engineer Margaret Hamilton Dies at 90
cards.content: Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering software engineer, has died at 90. She led a team of 100 engineers at MIT to design the software for NASA's Apollo missions, helping to land astronauts on the moon. Hamilton's work ensured mission success, including during the Apollo 11 mission, and she popularized the field of software engineering. She was honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 and received NASA's Exceptional Space Act Award in 2003. Her legacy will be honored at Draper Laboratory, where she worked, and her contributions to science and space travel will be remembered.

cards.title: Tennessee River Valley Hunters Inherited Stone Deposit Knowledge
cards.content: An analysis of 500 spear points suggests that Ice Age hunters in the Tennessee River Valley inherited knowledge of stone deposits to decide which tools were worth carrying. Hunters like the Clovis and Cumberland groups, who lived 13,200 years ago, would often leave behind usable stone spearheads, conserving resources and adapting to new environments. This study, published in the Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory, compares the tools left behind by these groups to investigate how knowledge of local resources influenced their decisions. The findings provide insights into the daily lives and resource management strategies of early hunter-gatherers.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Pennsylvania sees over 1,000 measles cases since April
cards.content: A massive measles outbreak in central Pennsylvania has caused significant pain and suffering to families, with over 1,000 cases reported since April. The Central Pennsylvania Clinic, a nonprofit serving children and adults with genetic disorders, is at the forefront of the response. The clinic's staff is focused on keeping patients safe and healthy, relying on trust built over years to provide accurate information and consistent messaging. Vaccination rates are critical, with the MMR vaccine being extremely effective. The clinic has hosted pop-up vaccination clinics, with nearly 200 events and thousands of doses administered since spring. Home visits and vaccinations are also increasing, with staff prioritizing patient care and safety.

cards.title: Nigerian Paediatrician Elected as UICC President-Elect
cards.content: Dr Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu, a Nigerian paediatrician, was elected as the president-elect of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), the first African to lead the organisation. She takes up the role as cancer cases and deaths are projected to rise sharply, with the greatest increases expected in poorer countries. Bagudu aims to reorient global cancer policy towards countries with limited cancer services and bridge the gap between countries with limited cancer services and the research, technology and treatments being developed elsewhere.

cards.title: WHO Reports Death of Plague Researcher Darya Shipilova at Russian Institute
cards.content: The World Health Organization (WHO) reported the death of a 28-year-old worker at a Russian institute that researched plague, sparking global concern. The worker, Darya Shipilova, died on October 2 from pneumonia of unknown origin. The WHO has few clear answers about the incident and is seeking more information from the Russian government. Currently, over 200 people who had contact with Shipilova are in quarantine or under close follow-up. The risk to the general public appears to be low, but WHO is continuing to monitor the situation.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: WWF Report Reveals Global Wildlife Decline, India Sees Species Growth
cards.content: A new report by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) found a 73% decline in monitored wildlife populations globally between 1970 and 2022, with habitat loss and degradation being the most frequently reported threats. However, India has recorded gains in the numbers of several major species, including tigers, greater one-horned rhinoceroses, Asiatic lions, and common leopards. The country's conservation efforts have been successful, with population increases among several species. The report highlights the importance of conservation measures, noting that declines in biodiversity cannot be reversed by conservation efforts alone.

cards.title: Heavy rain and snow hit northern India, thunderstorms warned
cards.content: Heavy rain and snowfall hit several Indian regions, including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, as strong winds swept across higher Himalayan peaks. Meanwhile, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Sikkim were placed under heavy rainfall alerts due to thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds. Delhi-NCR experienced cooler mornings and nights, but daytime temperatures remained high, with isolated thunderstorms and showers possible. Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh were warned of thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds. The southwest monsoon withdrawal progressed across India, signaling changing weather patterns and the gradual arrival of cooler conditions.

cards.title: India Expects Rain, Snow, Heat, and Thunderstorms
cards.content: Northern hills are expected to experience rain and snowfall, while Delhi and nearby plains face heat and humidity, with temperatures potentially dropping by 2-4 degrees Celsius in the coming days. Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand may receive rain, with higher mountain areas potentially witnessing light snowfall. Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are forecast to receive heavy rain, with a yellow alert issued by the weather department. Several states may also face thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds, with Pilani recording the country's highest temperature at 40.1 degrees Celsius.

sections.title: Entertainment

cards.title: Disney+ to air Super Bowl, Monday Night Football games to US subscribers
cards.content: {Disney has announced that its streaming service Disney+ will air the 2027 Super Bowl, as well as two Monday Night Football games, to all subscribers in the U.S. The game will also air on ESPN and ABC, with ad spots already sold out, the earliest sellout in Super Bowl history. This is part of Disney's efforts to expand its live sports streaming offerings, following the launch of a standalone ESPN streaming service and the addition of Formula E to Disney+. Other streamers, such as YouTube and Netflix, are also investing in live sports to bolster their portfolios.}

cards.title: Beverley Knight's Musical Sylvia Aims to Inspire Empowerment and Change
cards.content: Singer Beverley Knight hopes audiences watching her latest musical, Sylvia, will leave feeling empowered and believing their voices can make a difference. The musical tells the story of suffragette Sylvia Pankhurst and her family's rift caused by the fight for women's voting rights. Knight, who plays Emmeline Pankhurst, wants audiences to leave with a sense of empowerment and a connection to the story, which explores the suffragette movement from 1903 to 1928. The show features a mix of music genres, including R&B, funk, soul, garage, gospel, and house, and aims to inspire audiences to use their voices to effect change.

cards.title: New Play Explores Men's Mental Health through Boxing
cards.content: A new play, The Corner Man, explores men's mental health through the world of boxing, delving into the struggles of identity and purpose faced by athletes when their sport comes to an end. The play follows a boxer forced to confront life outside the ring after years of dedication. Writer and producer Cathal J Ferris draws from his own experience and conversations with fighters to examine the difficulties men have talking about their mental health and the importance of support networks.

cards.title: Alberta to Hold Independence Referendum on October 19
cards.content: The Canadian province of Alberta will hold a referendum on October 19, allowing residents to vote on independence. Keith Wilson, an independence supporter, believes the province's unique economy, rich in oil and gas, would thrive independently. However, opponents, including Premier Danielle Smith, predict significant costs and uncertainty, with estimates ranging from C$50bn to C$400bn. A report warns of a long and costly to-do list, including setting up agencies, developing a constitution, and negotiating national security. Opinion polling indicates around 20% to 25% of Albertans plan to vote in favour of independence.

cards.title: Royal Mail to cut 2,500 head office roles by end-2027
cards.content: Royal Mail plans to cut 2,500 head office and supporting roles by end-2027, representing 2% of its 131,000-strong workforce. The cuts aim to improve efficiency, with voluntary redundancies and people choosing to leave the company. The plan is in formal consultation with unions, despite concerns from the Communication Workers Union that the cuts will worsen the company's poor performance and delivery targets. The company has struggled to meet delivery targets and faces criticism from politicians and the public over slow letter deliveries.

cards.title: Weston Family Buys Boots for $8.9 Billion, Investing in Improved Experience
cards.content: Boots, the UK-based pharmacy and retail chain, has been sold to Canada's Weston family for $8.9 billion. The 177-year-old company, founded by John Boot in 1849, has expanded its business to sell health and beauty products, meal deals, and travel accessories. Despite challenges from rivals and changing shopping habits, Boots has performed well, generating £7.5 billion in sales in its most recent annual results. The Weston family plans to invest in the business, focusing on an improved shopping experience and expansion of healthcare services. The deal is set to be completed in early 2027.
